response: Menopausal hormone therapy (HT) has been associated with irregular endometrial bleeding, but the underlying mechanisms are not well understood. Research suggests that uterine natural killer (uNK) cells may play a role in regulating this bleeding. A study found that uNK cells and their associated cytokines may be involved in the development of irregular bleeding in postmenopausal women taking HT. This is the first report to demonstrate a possible mechanism by which HT may induce irregular bleeding, highlighting the potential importance of uNK cells in this process. However, more research is needed to fully understand the relationship between HT, uNK cells, and irregular endometrial bleeding.
